newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia eyes final word on Coporo oil by March.
newsitem.headline: Colombia eyes final word on Coporo oil by March.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol said it will take a final decision on the future of the Coporo prospect by the end of March in a document released Monday.
"Appraisal and interpretation of drill data, as well as the seven production test runs...will be made in the first quarter of 1997," Ecopetrol said in its monthly organ Carta Petrolera.
"Only at this stage when there is a calculation of probable reserves will Ecopetrol decide on future action in this structure," it added.

A number of conflicting reports have been issued about the viability of the Coporo structure in Colombia's eastern plains since President Ernesto Samper announced it contained minimum reserves of 700,000 barrels of crude amid great fanfare during a visit to New York in September.

Ecopetrol's then-chairman Luis Bernardo Florez appeared to give the final word in an interview in late December when he said there was "much less" than the forecast reserves of between 700,000 and 1.3 million barrels in Coporo and said the prospect was not commercially viable.

But last month, Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar revived the debate during a trip to the United States, raising reserve estimates to as high as 3 billion barrels and saying that the prospect could be opened up to private sector associates later this year.

In its Carta Petrolera, Ecopetrol said it had spent $60.5 million in studies and tests in Coporo and reiterated that before drilling, the well was estimated as having a 17 percent success rate -- about average for this area known known as the Llanos foothills.

Tests, however, in this region notorious for difficult drilling conditions, proved disheartening. Ecopetrol said low porosity rocks and the lack of gas or water to drive crude to the surface would make it virtually impossible to extract reserves.
Whatever the fate of Coporo, Ecopetrol stressed its commitment to continuing exploration in the Medina block.

"The foregoing does not mean Ecopetrol has decided to suspend its direct exploration program in the Llanos foothills. The company will continue to search for hydrocarbons in the Medina block and in the Villavicencio block," Carta Petrolera stated.
